desks.Dividends: Microsoft goes ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the raised quarterly rate declared Sep 15 (+7.7%, its 24th consecutive annual increase) — the only declared watchlist ex-date in the next four weeks. Apple's dividend is still undeclared, with a declaration expected alongside Nov 2 earnings; re-check Nov 3. SPY, QQQ, and Nvidia next go ex in December, outside the window, on UNVERIFIED estimates; Tesla pays no dividend. No cuts or specials announced.
desks.Earnings: Microsoft Wed Oct 28 after close is the week's binary event, on FOMC day, with its implied move resolved at ±5.26% (Oct 30 straddle $28.00 against $532.60); Nasdaq consensus is $4.71 (14 estimates, against $4.13 last year). Apple Mon Nov 2 after close follows with implied moves of ±4.26% (Nov 4 expiry) and ±4.73% (Nov 6 expiry); consensus is $2.00 (8 estimates, against $1.85). Historical average earnings-day moves over eight quarters are 4.04% for Microsoft and 1.98% for Apple. Tesla already reported Oct 21; Nvidia's date is unconfirmed, with trackers listing Nov 17, 18, and 25.
desks.Futures: Crude is pricing a geopolitical risk premium, not a confirmed supply shortfall: Brent held near $115 Monday after Friday's $116.72 settle, while Hormuz transit readings are sharply reduced but methodology-conflicted and reported as a range, not resolved. The EIA print shows a third straight crude draw of 3.1 million barrels, with distillates 9% below the five-year average. Natural gas storage rose 77 Bcf to 3,644 Bcf, near average. Next catalysts: EIA Wed Oct 28, EIA gas Thu Oct 29, WASDE Tue Nov 10.
desks.Parity: No new put-call or box parity violation found, and deterministic parity stands as the pricing constraint. The one methodology item: S&P Dow Jones Indices revises its growth/value style scoring — momentum drops from growth scoring, free cash flow, forward earnings, and intangible assets enter the value assessment — effective before the open Dec 21, 2026. That is a style-index reclassification, not a parity deviation, and per-name weight changes are UNVERIFIED. A secondhand estimate of $375 billion or more in passive funds tied to the affected benchmarks is an analyst estimate, not an S&P figure. FTSE Russell's separate growth-value consultation closes Dec 11 as a watch item only.
desks.Premium: Today's live close puts Microsoft's Oct 30 at-the-money implied volatility at 56.9% (call) and 55.7% (put) — event premium around the Oct 28 earnings inside that expiry, not a mispricing read, and premium into that binary is event premium by the standing rule. SPY and QQQ sit below realized volatility on the live basis and Tesla is roughly in line; Apple and Nvidia sit modestly above realized but are window-contingent (single-day variance shares of 36.4% and 31.0%, with QQQ at 32.0%), so no clean verdict is issued for those three. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names; no free IV-history source was available.
desks.Quant lab: Five candidates scored and appended to the ledger (#152-156), all ARCHIVE, none reaching TEST or INTEGRATE. The strongest, a GitHub options market-making and volatility-trading repo (#156, score 43), falls below the 45 WATCH band, has no tests or CI in its tree, and its code was not run. The four arXiv papers are pricing-numerics or market-making theory with no author code link, or, for the trading-agent paper, a framing mismatch with the paper-only boundary. No duplicates were added.

headline: Daily research brief — Monday, October 26

items.detail: Microsoft reports Wed Oct 28 after close, the same day as the FOMC decision at 2:00 p.m. ET, so the Oct 29 session move cannot be attributed to earnings alone. The implied move is now resolved at ±5.26%: the Oct 30-expiry at-the-money straddle at $28.00 against $532.60, matching the Oct 23 own calculation of 5.28% and retiring the stale 7.57% secondary read from Oct 18. That straddle embeds both the FOMC decision and earnings, so the full 5.26% is not an earnings-only read. The historical average earnings-day move for Microsoft over the last eight quarters is 4.04% on the same close-to-close method.
items.title: Wednesday pairs the Fed decision with Microsoft earnings

items.detail: FRED prints through Fri Oct 23 put the 10-year at 5.00% and the 2-year at 4.69%, a 2s10s spread of +31 basis points, down from 47 basis points on Aug 27. The compression is bear-flattening: the 2-year rose 49 basis points over 60 days against 33 for the 10-year. SOFR sits 4 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, showing no funding stress. Elevated long rates keep the discount-rate headwind on growth multiples in place into Wednesday's decision.
items.title: Rates stay high as the curve flattens into the Fed meeting

items.detail: Brent held near $115 Monday after Friday's $116.72 settle. Transit readings through the Strait of Hormuz are sharply reduced, but the sources use different methods and windows, so they are reported as a range, not a settled figure. Distillates remain the tight spot at 9% below the five-year average into heating season, while natural gas storage at 3,644 Bcf sits near average. The next EIA petroleum print lands Wed Oct 28 at 10:30 a.m. ET, hours before the FOMC statement.
